solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Succeeded in typing novel, no need for new pen

indicators.note: the in-word sits inside the rest, so the succeeded letter goes into the reworked letters
novel as an adjective means new and fresh, so the letters of typing are rearranged
no need for says a letter is dispensed with and dropped from the jumble

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for succeeded, as in family trees

explanation.surface: A typist manages fine and decides a new pen is not required after all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' shuffles TYPING, 'no need for' drops its N to leave letters for PIGTY, and 'in' puts S inside them.
explanation.definitionFit: A pen is an enclosure for animals, and a sty is the enclosure where pigs are kept.

clue.text: Region for French wine roughly north of Spain

indicators.note: in a down clue a piece north of another is written above it, so it comes first

parts.note: pro is Latin-derived for 'in favour of', so for gives PRO
vin is the French word for wine
C is circa, Latin for roughly or about
E is the international vehicle code for Spain (España)

explanation.surface: A travel note: a wine region of France lying roughly north of Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: A province is an administrative region or territory of a country.

clue.text: Resentment when overlooking river and lifting no fish

indicators.note: overlooking here means ignoring or leaving out, so the river letter is dropped

parts.note: a grudge is lingering resentment

indicators.note: lifting in a down clue raises the word so it reads bottom to top, reversing it

explanation.surface: Someone bitter by a river, refusing to hoist anything, perhaps an angler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overlooking' takes R from GRUDGE to leave GUDGE; 'lifting' turns NO into ON.
explanation.definitionFit: The gudgeon is a small freshwater fish of the carp family, used as bait.

clue.text: Subject that man to replace one in prison sentence

indicators.note: to replace says one piece is swapped out and the other put in its place

parts.note: doing time means serving a prison sentence
I is the Roman numeral for one
he is the pronoun for that man

explanation.surface: A legal topic: a man stepping in for someone else to serve a jail term.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to replace' puts HE where I stood in TIME, giving T-HE-ME.
explanation.definitionFit: A theme is the subject or topic of a talk, essay or piece of art.

clue.text: Others work on stone area beside highway

indicators.note: in an across clue the work placed on stone follows it

parts.note: the rest means the others
ST is the abbreviation for stone, the British unit of weight
OP is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: Other labourers working on stone in a lay-by next to the road.
explanation.definitionFit: A rest stop is a place off a highway where drivers pull over for a break.

clue.text: Characters from house state a gent sacked workers in property

indicators.note: Characters from says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Office gossip: a man sacked by some house in the property trade.
explanation.walkthrough: The run starts with the last two letters of 'house' and ends with the first of 'sacked'.
explanation.definitionFit: Estate agents are the British name for real-estate brokers who sell and let property.

clue.text: Cheers, endlessly raving over director

parts.note: ta is British informal thanks, like cheers

indicators.note: endlessly says the last letter is cut off

parts.note: raving and ranting both mean shouting wildly
O is the cricket scorebook abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: A toast, then unending ravings about a film director.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts the G from RANTING.
explanation.definitionFit: Quentin Tarantino is the American film-maker of Pulp Fiction and Kill Bill.

clue.text: Cast nick the set

indicators.note: cast as in casting metal or dice, throwing the letters into a new shape

explanation.surface: A director's note: the actor called Nick is cast on the film set.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cast' shuffles NICKTHE.
explanation.definitionFit: A sauce or jelly that sets becomes firm; to thicken is to stiffen in that way.

clue.text: Trouble with crack climbing ornamental structure

indicators.note: climbing in a down clue makes the letters read upward, so they are reversed

parts.note: ado is fuss or trouble
a gap is a crack or opening

explanation.surface: Climbing a decorative tower is hard because of a crack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climbing' turns ADOGAP into PAGODA.
explanation.definitionFit: A pagoda is a tiered tower, often temple-like, used as ornament in gardens.

clue.text: Many artistic works lacking head

indicators.note: lacking head says the first letter is dropped

parts.note: doodles are idle sketches, humorously called artistic works

explanation.surface: Plenty of pictures with no headings, or with the heads missing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking head' takes D off DOODLES.
explanation.definitionFit: Oodles is informal for a great quantity, so it serves as lots or many.

clue.text: Lively prison gang

parts.note: stir is slang for prison
a ring is a gang, as in a drugs ring

explanation.surface: A spirited band of convicts in a jail.
explanation.definitionFit: Stirring means rousing or exciting, so it fits as a description of something animated.

clue.text: They seek those gifted money of old troop members

parts.note: the talent was an ancient unit of weight and money
Scouts are organised in troops

explanation.surface: Old money and boy scouts on the hunt for gifted youngsters.
explanation.definitionFit: Talent scouts look for promising performers or athletes to recruit.

clue.text: Clumsy removing wings, dined on insect

indicators.note: wings are the outer letters, so taking them off leaves the inside

parts.note: in cricket the on side is also called the leg side
an ant is an insect

explanation.surface: A clumsy diner pulls the wings off before eating a bug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'removing wings' leaves INE from 'dined'. LEG for 'on' is cricket: the on side of the field is the leg side.
explanation.definitionFit: Inelegant means lacking grace, which is awkward or clumsy.

clue.text: Blatant denial youngster vocalised

indicators.note: vocalised says the words are spoken and heard, not written

parts.note: nay is an old word of denial, meaning no; a kid is a youngster

explanation.surface: A child says no openly, the denial spoken out loud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vocalised' says NAY plus KID is heard as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Naked ambition or a naked lie is undisguised, obvious and unashamed.

clue.text: Damaged sections in road creating concerns

indicators.note: damaged suggests something broken up, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Potholed stretches of road give the council worries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Damaged' shuffles SECTIONSINROAD.
explanation.definitionFit: Considerations are factors to weigh up, things that are matters of concern.

clue.text: Strengthened vessels from old cairns tidied up

indicators.note: tidied up means rearranged into order, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Armoured ships built from tidied stone piles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tidied up' shuffles OLDCAIRNS.
explanation.definitionFit: Ironclads were nineteenth-century warships protected by iron armour plates.

clue.text: Yielded when given perfume, having rejected charmer origi- nally

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as he left'

indicators.note: having rejected says a letter is thrown out

parts.note: something given perfume is scented

indicators.note: originally points to the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Someone gave in once perfumed, after turning down a charmer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having rejected' takes C, the first letter of 'charmer', out of SCENTED.
explanation.definitionFit: To assent is to agree or give way, so assented means gave in.

clue.text: Classic book campaign that might involve Narnia and Never- land

definitions.meaning: H G Wells's 1898 novel of Martian invasion

definitions.text: campaign that might involve Narnia and Never- land
definitions.meaning: a war between fictional worlds such as Narnia and Neverland

explanation.surface: A classic novel about a war fought between the lands of children's fantasy.
explanation.walkthrough: Narnia and Neverland are the imaginary worlds of C S Lewis and J M Barrie.
explanation.definitionFit: Wells's novel is a classic; a campaign fought between such realms would literally be a conflict of worlds.

clue.text: A wind in Utah regularly avoided US city

indicators.note: in says the wind goes inside the other letters
regularly avoided means every other letter is skipped

parts.note: a gust is a blast of wind

explanation.surface: A wind in Utah steered around an American city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly avoided' means skipping alternate letters of Utah, keeping the first and third; 'in' then places the wind between those two.
explanation.definitionFit: Augusta is the capital of Maine and a city in Georgia, famed for golf.

clue.text: Tiling ground above base that's rock

indicators.note: in a down clue the piece above another comes first
ground is the past of grind, crushed, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: e is the base of natural logarithms in maths

explanation.surface: Tiles crushed above a floor that is made of stone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ground' shuffles TILING; E for base is from mathematics.
explanation.definitionFit: Lignite is brown coal, a soft sedimentary rock.

clue.text: Balls in golf hit higher than opponents

parts.note: G is golf in the NATO phonetic alphabet
a lob is a shot hit high into the air
in bridge East and South are opponents, giving E and S

explanation.surface: Golf balls struck higher than those of rival players.
explanation.walkthrough: E and S, East and South, are opposing partnerships at bridge.
explanation.definitionFit: Globes are spheres, round objects like balls.

clue.text: Reason I choke after cycling

indicators.note: cycling moves letters round from the front to the back

parts.note: to clog is to choke or block

explanation.surface: A cyclist explains why they choke after riding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cycling' moves IC from the front of ICLOG to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Logic is reasoning, and reason in the sense of sound thinking.

clue.text: EU act with goal to transform record

indicators.note: to transform is to change shape, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A Brussels law aimed at reshaping the way records are kept.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to transform' shuffles EUACTGOAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A catalogue is a list or register, a recorded inventory.

clue.text: Uncovered blade on the French kitchen utensil

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece on another sits above it
uncovered strips off the first and last letters

parts.note: le is French for the

explanation.surface: A bare knife lying beside a French kitchen tool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uncovered' takes B and E off 'blade'.
explanation.definitionFit: A ladle is a deep long-handled spoon for serving soup.

clue.text: Vehicle with tow at back showing strain

parts.note: a bus is a vehicle

indicators.note: back says the letters run backwards

parts.note: a tug tows boats, and to tug is to tow

explanation.surface: A van towing at the rear looks strained.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns TUGAT into TAGUT.
explanation.definitionFit: To bust a gut is an idiom for working or straining extremely hard.

clue.text: Commercial opening not secure

parts.note: an ad is a commercial
a rift is a gap or opening

explanation.surface: A shaky opening for a television advert.
explanation.definitionFit: A boat adrift is unmoored, loose and not fastened.

clue.text: Analyses to cut stone that's least dense

indicators.note: the analysing word cuts into the stone abbreviation, splitting it

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for stone, the British weight
to parse is to analyse grammatically

explanation.surface: A mason studies where to cut the lightest stone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to cut' puts PARSES between S and T.
explanation.definitionFit: Sparsest means most thinly spread, the opposite of densest.

clue.text: A space festival is epic

parts.note: an en is a printer's space, half an em
Eid is a Muslim festival

explanation.surface: A space festival hailed as epic.
explanation.walkthrough: EN is printing jargon for a space.
explanation.definitionFit: The Aeneid is Virgil's Latin epic poem about Aeneas.
